reddit.title: One fact, two sources: avoiding duplicate study cards
reddit.content:
If a textbook chapter and a lecture transcript state the same fact, generating a fresh note from each upload splits the learner's review history.

A safer model:

1. Keep the original front and back.
2. Normalize a separate matching projection.
3. Use an exact key for retries and formatting differences.
4. Use fuzzy search only to shortlist paraphrases.
5. Attach page and timestamp evidence to one accepted fact.
6. Update the same Anki note instead of exporting a new one.

I wrote out the SQLite schema, transaction boundary, deletion semantics, and test cases here:
https://blog.lazying.art/?p=3782&utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=profile&utm_campaign=card_dedup

Disclosure: I maintain the linked guide and the public project patterns it references.
reddit.policy: First-party profile resource only. It is not a generated reply in a community thread and contains a concise maintainer disclosure.

instagram.policy: Do not turn a database design article into a generic graphic. Wait for a real, rights-cleared before-and-after study artifact.

hackernews.policy: Do not post agent-authored comments or submit the article without an independently relevant discussion.

limits: The public repositories demonstrate source, hierarchy, and knowledge-identity patterns; they do not implement the complete deduplication workflow described in the article.
Fuzzy similarity creates review candidates only until labeled tests support a safer decision boundary.
